Ken Krawchuk

Libertarian candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Pennsylvania · Challenger

Founder and president of Amendment 16 Ltd., an information technology consulting firm; business architect

Ken Krawchuk, of Abington Township in Montgomery County, is the Libertarian Party nominee for Governor of Pennsylvania in the November 3, 2026 general election. His running mate for lieutenant governor is John Thomas. He was the Libertarian nominee for governor in 1998, 2002 and 2018, and he has also run for the state House, the U.S. House and Abington Township Commissioner.

Where Krawchuk stands

Education and school choice
Proposes replacing Pennsylvania's traditional public school funding model with education savings accounts that families could use for private school tuition. He supports privatizing the public school system.
Property taxes / public education funding
Proposes eliminating school property taxes. His campaign argues that privatizing schools would make this possible.
Revenue proposals / income tax
Proposes eliminating the state personal income tax over the course of one term.
State budget and spending
Says he would veto tax increases and use the line-item veto to remove spending he considers unnecessary.
Public assistance
Proposes requiring people who receive state funding to reapply for assistance during a governor's four-year term.
Elections and voter ID
Supports eliminating mail-in ballots and expanding voter ID requirements.
Criminal justice and drug policy
Supports decriminalizing drugs and ending parole for people convicted of violent crimes.

Background

  • Libertarian nominee for Pennsylvania Governor, 2026
  • Libertarian nominee for Pennsylvania Governor, 1998, 2002 and 2018 (49,229 votes in 2018)
  • Sought the Libertarian nomination for U.S. Vice President, 2000 (placed third)
  • Ran for Pennsylvania state House (including 1994), U.S. House and Abington Township Commissioner
  • Former chair of the Libertarian Party of Pennsylvania
  • Registered Libertarian since 1993
  • Founder and president of Amendment 16 Ltd., an IT consulting firm
  • B.S. in physics, Saint Joseph's University, 1975
  • Graduate of Cardinal Dougherty High School, Philadelphia

Also running for Governor and Lieutenant Governor

  • Josh Shapiro Democratic
  • Stacy Garrity Republican
